activities.anchor: roughly matching all natural terrestrial fixation
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the doubled nitrogen cycle
activities.name: hieNitrogenEstimate

config.prompt: Haber–Bosch fixation adds ~150 million tonnes of reactive nitrogen per year, roughly matching all natural terrestrial fixation. Combined, about how many million tonnes now enter the biosphere each year?
config.why: ~150 natural + ~150 industrial ≈ 300 million tonnes — humanity has doubled the nitrogen cycle, a bigger perturbation of a global cycle than the carbon one.
config.context: The bill arrives three ways: the oxygen sag in fresh water, coastal dead zones in the sea, and nitrous oxide (~300× the warming power of CO₂ per molecule).

activities.anchor: strip the soil of specific minerals
activities.caption: file the ledger — engines and their bill
activities.name: hieCostBuckets

config.prompt: Every entry below belongs on one side of the food-supply ledger. File it:

items.label: 10 kg of feed per kg of cattle live-weight gain
selective breeding of crops and livestock
meat using ~80% of agricultural land for under 20% of calories

config.why: The engines tripled cereal yields between 1960 and 2000; the bill arrives as stripped soil, pest build-up, reduced biodiversity and a trophic-arithmetic land footprint.

activities.anchor: a forest cut into patches carries a long
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the fragmentation answer
activities.name: hieFragmentSpot

config.prompt: This habitat-fragmentation answer contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: The species–area relationship is S = c·A^z, with z near 0.25 for islands and habitat fragments.
Shrink the habitat tenfold and it retains 10^−0.25 ≈ 56% of its species — a 44% loss.
Fragmentation matters as much as acreage, not less.
Patches keep losing species for decades after the chainsaws stop — the extinction debt.
Corridors therefore look pleasant but are mathematically unnecessary.
Every food web the removed forest supported simplifies from the bottom up.
config.correction: Corridors are a mathematical NECESSITY, not a nicety — arrangement matters as much as area.
config.why: The same species–area curve that turns tenfold shrinkage into a 44% loss is why reconnecting patches is the required fix, not a decoration.

activities.caption: same hectare, different worlds — tropical vs elsewhere
activities.name: hieTropicCompare

config.prompt: One hectare of forest cleared — drag the divider between the two accounting entries:

before.label: a hectare elsewhere
before.text: Real species lost, real soil exposed — but the regional species pool is thinner, so the unique evolutionary history removed is smaller.

after.label: a tropical hectare
after.text: Tropical forest holds over half of terrestrial species on ~10% of land area — this hectare removes more unique evolutionary history (EDGE logic) than a hectare anywhere else.

config.why: That structural asymmetry is why tropical deforestation dominates the biodiversity bill, with ~10 million hectares lost per year through the 2010s (FAO).

activities.caption: pin the kill threshold on the oxygen scale
activities.name: hieSagPlace

config.prompt: The widget's red line marks ~5 mg/L, where many fish are stressed. Below a lower threshold, most die — place it on the scale (mg/L dissolved oxygen):
config.why: Below ~2 mg/L, most fish die — which is why monitoring teams read BOD upstream and down plus indicator species to locate the sag.
config.context: Mayfly larvae need clean water; tubifex worms tolerate the worst.

activities.caption: pair each monitoring signal with what it reports
activities.name: hieIndicatorMatch

config.prompt: A monitoring team reads four signals downstream of an outfall. Pair each with its meaning:
config.why: Indicator species, BOD and the sag's recovery distance are exactly the signature teams read — in the sea, the same nutrient subsidy draws the Baltic and Mississippi-driven dead zones.

activities.anchor: added faster than the carbon cycle absorbs
activities.caption: true or false — pollutants and treaties
activities.name: hiePollutionJudge

statements.s: Non-biodegradable plastics fragment into microplastics, are ingested by animals and never rot away.
statements.why: That persistence is the problem — smothered soil, entangled and choked marine life.

statements.s: CFCs were identified by chemistry as the ozone cause before the ozone hole was measured.
statements.why: The order ran the other way: 1985 measurements found the hole, then chemistry identified CFCs, then the 1987 protocol phased them out.

statements.s: Methane and CO₂ drive climate change when added faster than the carbon cycle absorbs them.
statements.why: They strengthen the enhanced greenhouse effect, shifting rainfall and melting ice.

statements.s: The ozone layer is healing because the Montreal Protocol phased out CFCs.
statements.why: The one global atmospheric problem solved end to end — a decisive measurement bought a fast treaty.

config.root: A species is down to a few dozen individuals in one shrinking habitat, and it is losing genetic variation.

start.text: What is the first conservation move?

choices.label: Start a captive breeding programme
choices.feedback: Supplement tools apply: artificial insemination and IVF join the toolkit.

choices.label: Bank seeds in a seed bank
choices.feedback: Seed banks suit plants — for animals you need the living population managed.

choices.label: Leave it alone; nature will cope
choices.feedback: Small populations keep losing variation — fragile against disease and change.

bred.text: The genetics rule of thumb: ~50 effective breeders to dodge inbreeding depression, ~500 to hold adaptive variation. The programme is running — next?

choices.label: Protect habitat and release
choices.feedback: Captive breeding only pays off if the freed animals have somewhere to live.

choices.label: Keep every individual in captivity permanently
choices.feedback: Insurance, but no ecosystem function — and the gene pool stays small.

seeded.text: Banked — but this is an animal, and seed banks store plants. The population genetics (50/500) still needs managing in the flesh.

watch.text: Monitored decline is not conservation: the remedies list is monitoring, education, captive breeding, seed banks — then acting on them.

released.text: Back in a protected habitat, with the 500-breeders target keeping adaptive variation in the population.

zoo.text: A living archive, not a recovered species — conservation aims at populations in ecosystems.

config.why: Endangered species face climate change, habitat destruction, hunting, overharvesting, pollution and introduced species — the remedies are practical, and small populations lose the variation that makes them robust.
